authors: James L. Bischoff, Robert J. Rosenbauer, Kenneth S. Pitzer
title: The system NaCl-H2O: Relations of vapor-liquid near the critical temperature of water and of vapor-liquid-halite from 300 to 500 C
experimental_method: Titanium vessel of 26 ml in a fluidized particle bath; vapor sampled sequentially from the top and liquid from the bottom while pressure fell along the phase boundary (T near Tc), or three samples of vapor from the vapor-liquid-halite assemblage; chloride analysed by ion chromatography with conductivity detector.
uncertainties_stated: T = 373.0 and 375.5 C (+-0.1 C) for the isotherms; background contamination about 0.5 ppm Cl, lowest reported value 4 ppm Cl (0.00071 % NaCl); no other uncertainties.
quality_remarks: Authors report vapor NaCl contents of the three-phase assemblage far above those of Sourirajan and Kennedy (1962) above 410 C. Table 3 values were read from figures. Tables concern the NaCl-H2O vapor-liquid(-halite) equilibrium, which sits at the edge of the project's scope (vapor-side salt content, no gas component); extracted for the builder to decide.
